question: Does no scheduled expiry justify replaying a perpetual until a researcher-selected horizon when the venue terminates trading, and can last trade substitute for settlement index averaging?
hypothesis: A verified delisting rule can force a distinct exit event and price role; perpetual label alone does not guarantee horizon continuity.
falsifier: Official termination rules guarantee continuation to original horizon or explicitly equate settlement to last trade; no source implies unknown rather than support.
scope: Enabled BTC/ETH/AAPL/QQQ relevance only; other delisted symbols may be documentary examples, never target economic data or enabled products.
novelty: Exchange product termination event and settlement averaging, distinct from corporate-action unit rebasing, ADL and ordinary order fill; prior corporate-action mention of delisting disclosed.
comparison: No-expiry implies uninterrupted holding / last trade proxy
Explicit exchange termination with event-specific price and fees
data_role: Official rule/announcement pages retrieved now, not contemporaneous price path; no API.
search_stop: Read global official general delisting settlement rule and at most two first relevant dated official announcements; stop when rule contrast and target-data gap resolved; no repeated searches absent new evidence.
fixed_arithmetic: price_component=q*(mean(index)-entry), proxy=q*(terminal_index-entry); equal-weight toy samples NOT official TWAP sampling
costs: Excluded from toy price component; actual_net null. Rule-specific delivery fee waiver must not imply all fees/funding/slippage zero.
completion: 6 frozen toy cases, hand unit checks, official source-role finding plus target admissibility gap; no economic plan or profitability selection
feedback: Adopt exact price roles/time/cost unknown boundaries from both full reviews; retain existing one feedback successor; independent root not feedback duplicate
old_BTC: Original windows ended; DATA_REQUIRED/METHOD_REQUIRED, not future wait
AB: PREPARATION_ONLY; no launch before real cost-review/feedback/web gates
